case_title: Bharat Kumar Rameshchandra Barot v. State of Gujarat
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Code of Criminal Procedure s.377
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine
neutral_facts: The accused was prosecuted for the murder of the deceased, Dilipbhai Ratnaji. The trial court convicted him for the offence punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to 10 years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 5000. The State filed an appeal under Section 377 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seeking enhancement of the sentence. The High Court allowed the appeal and increased the sentence to life imprisonment. The accused did not appear in the appeal despite being served with notice, and no appeal was filed challenging the conviction. The High Court appointed an amicus curiae to represent the accused. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, stating that the Sessions Judge's sentence of 10 years was illegal as it did not conform to the punishment prescribed under Section 302 IPC, which mandates either death, life imprisonment, or a fine.
